title: Optional chaining and nullish coalescing
runtime: Modern evergreen browser or Node.js with ES modules. Run fragments in browser DevTools or a small .js file unless the example says otherwise.

objectives.text: Stop a property chain only for null or undefined.
Use optional access, calls, and indexes.
Use ?? when only missing values need a fallback.
Combine access and fallback without hiding bad data.

learningFlow: Explain the result in your own words
Apply the idea in a different problem
Review after two and seven days

sections.title: Optional chaining
sections.body: user.profile?.name returns undefined when profile is null or undefined instead of throwing. It does not hide an undeclared root variable, and it does not treat 0, false, or an empty string as missing. Place ?. at each uncertain step that needs protection.

sections.title: Property, call, and index forms
sections.body: obj?.property checks the object, obj.method?.() checks whether the method value is nullish, and list?.[0] checks before indexing. The chain short-circuits only along one continuous optional chain. Grouping can end that protection before later property access.

sections.title: Nullish coalescing
sections.body: value ?? fallback uses the fallback only when value is null or undefined. value || fallback also replaces 0, false, and an empty string, which may be valid settings or user input. Choose the operator from the product meaning of missing data.

sections.title: Safe reads with meaningful defaults
sections.body: const city = user.address?.city ?? "Unknown" safely reads an optional path and provides a display fallback. This does not validate the shape or fix malformed data. Validate important API data at the boundary, and use optional syntax only where absence is expected.

sections.title: Why this matters in React
sections.body: Optional chaining and nullish coalescing is part of the JavaScript model React code already uses. Components, event handlers, state updates, list rendering, and data requests become easier to reason about when this concept is understood without framework shortcuts. Practise the JavaScript behavior first, then identify the same rule in JSX or a component.
